title: North Carolina's 11th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The general election for North Carolina's 11th Congressional District pits Republican incumbent Chuck Edwards against Democratic nominee Jamie Ager. The district covers most of Western North Carolina, including Asheville and Hendersonville, and was redrawn in October 2025 under a new map. The race is considered the most competitive congressional contest in the state after redistricting, with the Cook Political Report rating it 'Likely Republican' and Inside Elections shifting it toward Democrats. Key issues include the pace of federal Hurricane Helene recovery funding, affordability for working families, and healthcare access, with Democrats hoping to capitalize on recent trending toward their party in the region.
polling_note: No public general election polls were found for this race as of the research date. Available polling data pertains only to the March 3 primary contests.

candidates.name: Chuck Edwards
candidates.summary: Chuck Edwards is the incumbent U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 11th Congressional District, first elected in 2022 after defeating then-Rep. Madison Cawthorn in the Republican primary. A former McDonald's franchisee and business consultant, Edwards previously served in the North Carolina Senate from 2016 to 2023. He serves on the House Appropriations and Budget Committees and has faced controversy including a House Ethics Committee investigation over sexual harassment allegations reported in April 2026.

candidates.name: Jamie Ager
candidates.summary: Jamie Ager is a fourth-generation farmer and small business owner from Fairview, North Carolina, and the Democratic nominee for the 11th Congressional District. He runs Hickory Nut Gap Farm, a sustainable meat company employing 25 people and working with dozens of regional farms. Ager comes from a politically active family — his grandfather Jamie Clarke represented the 11th District in Congress in the 1980s, his father served in the state House, and his brother Eric currently holds that state House seat. He won the Democratic primary on March 3, 2026 with nearly 65% of the vote and has been endorsed by the DCCC's 'Red to Blue' program.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this race, so the forecast relies entirely on non-polling indicators. Incumbent Chuck Edwards (R) benefits from incumbency and a district that, even after a pro-competitive 2025 redraw, still carries a Republican lean reflected in Cook's 'Likely Republican' rating. However, multiple factors introduce significant uncertainty: the redistricting has made this the most competitive congressional race in North Carolina; Democratic nominee Jamie Ager is a strong, well-funded challenger with deep local roots and DCCC 'Red to Blue' backing; Edwards faces an active House Ethics Committee investigation (sexual harassment allegations, April 2026); Inside Elections has shifted the race toward Democrats; and regional trends are moving in the Democratic direction. Without polling to validate these dynamics, the Republican advantage is modest and confidence is low. Slight downward adjustment from the prior forecast reflects the ethics investigation and the district's increased competitiveness under the new map.
